Today the agency announced that a new country has joined the international agreement governing peaceful exploration of the Moon, bringing the total number of signatories to sixty. The signing took place at a ceremony in the capital, attended by senior officials from both governments. The agreement establishes shared principles for transparency, interoperability, and the safe conduct of operations on and around the lunar surface. “This signing reflects a common commitment to responsible exploration,” the administrator said. “Every new partner strengthens the framework that allows all of us to work together safely.” Signatories pledge to share scientific data publicly, to avoid harmful interference with each other’s activities, and to preserve heritage sites. The agency noted that participation does not require any country to contribute hardware, and that more than a dozen additional nations are in discussions about joining over the coming year.
